Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can land the right proposal: 

Summary of your requirements (please correct me if I'm off):
- Production datasets (PII) must reside in the EU (GDPR) for euro customers.
- Non-prod/dev tooling can remain in the US (no PII).
- You want regional pinning for model endpoints (ensure inference runs in-region).
- Cross-region failover acceptable only as a controlled, auditable fallback — prefer manual failover or opt-in automated failover with prior consent.
- Backups: encrypted at rest; ideally replicated to a secondary region but NOT across a legal boundary without explicit approval.
- Audit/logging: 1) retention policy for request logs; 2) access controls and KMS for key separation.

Attachments: sending our short whitepaper on region pinning and an internal note from product on available controls (redwood-data-residency-whitepaper.pdf, ma-ps-approved.txt).

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Do you need persistent backups stored in the EU exclusively (even for DR copies), or is encrypted replication to a nearby non-EU DR region acceptable if legal approves?
2) For logs/audit trails, what is the minimum retention you need and which logs must be stored in the EU? (request metadata vs full request/response)
3) Would FinnovA require dedicated KMS keys per customer/region (we support customer-managed keys) or is platform-managed KMS acceptable?

Next steps I propose:
- I will send a concise proposal of the configuration options (region pin + backup policy + failover behavior) and a recommended default that aligns with your legal ask.
- If it looks good, we can schedule a 30–45m technical breakout with FinnovA security to go through controls and DocuSign the DPA addendum.

Would you like that technical session this week or early next week?

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the docs. Helpful. Quick answers below and a couple of ask items for the security team: 

Confirmations: 
- Production (customer PII) must remain in the EU for all EU customers. No cross-border storage of that PII without legal approval.
- Non-prod/dev environments can be US. We will sanitize datasets before moving anything outside the EU.

Failover policy: 
- Prefer region-pinning for normal operations.
- For failover, we want an opt-in asynchronous cross-region failover; default should be disabled. If we opt in, failover must be logged, alerted to our security contacts, and require a documented justification.

Backups: 
- Backups containing PII must be stored only in the EU. We may accept an additional encrypted DR copy in a third EU region, but not in the US.

Logs and retention: 
- We need request metadata and error logs retained for 365 days in the EU. We do NOT want full request/response bodies stored outside the EU.

KMS: 
- We prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) per environment/region where feasible. If Redwood has a managed option, we need the ability to rotate and revoke keys on demand.

Security team, tagging you on cc — please add anything I've missed. We can do the tech deep-dive on Thu or Mon next week.

Thanks,
Olivia

Marissa / Karthik — internal notes and recommended configuration to respond to FinnovA's asks. Paste below for the email we'll send back (I can take the tech deep-dive if you want).

Key capabilities we can offer today: 
- Region pinning: endpoint-level region pinning supported. We can pin model endpoints to a single region (EU) so inference happens in-region for EU customers.
- Cross-region failover: we support two modes — manual failover (customer-initiated) and optional automated failover with a customer-configured policy. Both modes are auditable (logs + alert hooks). Automated failover is opt-in per endpoint.
- Backups: encrypted at rest using AES-256. We support region-scoped backups; for EU production PII we can configure backups to remain in EU regions only. We also support encrypted asynchronous replication to another EU region for DR.
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported (we integrate with common KMS providers). Keys can be scoped per environment/region; rotation and revocation supported.
- Logging & retention: request metadata and error logs can be retained for 365 days in-region. Full request/response bodies (containing PII) can be excluded from long-term storage or redacted on ingest.

Recommended proposal to FinnovA: 
1) Endpoint configuration: pin production endpoints to eu-west-1 (example) for EU customers.
2) Backups: enable encrypted backups with replication to a secondary EU region (eu-west-2) only.
3) Failover: default to manual failover; offer automated failover as opt-in (with audit trail and notification).
4) Keys & logs: CMK per environment (EU-prod), 365-day metadata retention, redact or avoid storing full request bodies outside EU.

I suggest we send a one-page configuration summary to FinnovA security and offer a 45-minute tech session. Legal should prepare a short DPA addendum reflecting backup/replication constraints.
